title: Personal Checking: inactivity period and dormant account fee by tier
content:
## Scope

This card gives, for each Personal Checking tier, the number of calendar months without customer-initiated activity after which the account becomes dormant, and the fee per statement cycle while the account is dormant. The dormant account fee never takes the balance below zero.

## Dormancy terms by tier

| Tier | Inactivity period before dormancy (calendar months without customer-initiated activity) | Dormant account fee per statement cycle (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 12 | 0.00 |
| Student Checking | 12 | 0.00 |
| Everyday Checking | 12 | 5.00 |
| Interest Checking | 12 | 5.00 |
| Premier Checking | 12 | 5.00 |
| Private Client Checking | 24 | 0.00 |

## Basis Q&A

**Q: Which tier allows the longest period of inactivity?**
A: Private Client Checking, at 24 calendar months; every other tier uses 12.

**Q: Which tiers charge while dormant?**
A: Everyday, Interest and Premier Checking, at 5.00 USD per statement cycle. Access, Student and Private Client Checking show 0.00.

**Hypothetical balance case**: a dormant Everyday Checking account holds 3.20 USD at cycle close. Because the dormant account fee never takes the balance below zero, the fee for that cycle cannot exceed 3.20 USD even though the tier figure is 5.00 USD.
